title: Customer security requirements rapid-assessment playbook and evidence templates
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary: Create a compact 'Rapid Assessment' playbook and a set of reusable evidence templates to accelerate triage of enterprise security & compliance asks (SOC2/ISO/HIPAA/GDPR/DPA/vendor questionnaires). The goal is to reduce mean time-to-response for prioritized intake by 40% and to standardize ask handling between PM, Security, and Solutions Engineering teams.

Problem: Incoming security questionnaires and DPA edits vary widely in completeness and scope. Current intake is ad hoc—SEs spend time re-gathering the same artifacts and Security Ops performs custom analysis per request. This causes long response timelines and inconsistent prioritization.

Scope: Deliverables include: 1) a one-page assessment rubric (risk x customer value x effort), 2) prioritized evidence template library (SOC2 controls mapping, encryption/KMS checklist, data residency artifacts, HIPAA table), 3) a decision script for ‘fast-track’ vs ‘deeper review’, 4) a triage playbook for Solutions Engineers with canned email responses, and 5) short training session + examples for SE/CS.

Out of scope: Building automated questionnaire parser (future project), changes to legal contract templates, or full audit readiness for new regions.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Playbook doc exists in Confluence with clear steps and owner for each decision path; 2) Evidence templates (Word/PDF) for SOC2, ISO, HIPAA, GDPR/DPA present and linked; 3) Triage rubric validated with Security and two SEs and annotated with 3 example customer cases; 4) Pilot run with 3 live customer requests reduces average initial response time by >=30%; 5) Hand-off checklist created for Security Ops and CS. All artifacts linked from ticket.
comments: 2025-02-18 - Ava Chen: Initial ticket created after weekly security intake sync. Noted recurring pain: SEs re-upload the same artifacts multiple times and inconsistent prioritization between product and security.

2025-02-21 - Mateo Alvarez: Scoped initial rubric; proposing a 3x3 matrix: Risk (Low/Medium/High) x Customer Value (Strategic/Standard/Low) x Effort (Quick/Moderate/Deep). Quick = <4 engineer hours or available artifact. Will draft examples.

2025-02-25 - Security (Priya Rao): Reviewed draft rubric. Suggested weighting to prioritize data residency and encryption items higher for EU customers. Requested adding KMS/HSM proof checklist. Marked security_review_required.

2025-02-27 - SE (Jordan Kim): Provided three recent customer questionnaires for test-cases (AcmeCorp, MediHealth, EuroBank). Recommended prebuilt canned responses for common asks to reduce back-and-forth.
2025-03-01 - Mateo Alvarez: First-pass Confluence doc published (link below) and uploaded evidence templates to Drive. Asked Legal to confirm DPA clause mapping for two items (awaiting response).

2025-03-03 - Cross-team meeting notes: Agreement to pilot with top 20 enterprise prospects. Action items: (1) Security to sign off on templates by 2025-03-07; (2) SEs to trial playbook for all new intake requests during pilot; (3) PM to run a before/after timing comparison.

2025-03-04 - Ava Chen: Updated acceptance criteria with measurable pilot target. Added dependency on ENG-1842 for an internal evidence storage API that will make the templates easier to attach to responses.
Planned next steps: finalize templates with Security and Legal review, record 30-minute training for SE team, and schedule pilot intake channel with CS Ops.
Risks: Legal DPA clarifications may require additional evidence beyond templates; if evidence storage API delivery slips, SEs will use Drive links temporarily (manual).
